about: Note scripts rendered by engines/build/fm1-render, by the app layer natively (tests/test_sim_web.py) and by the WebAssembly module under Node (sim/web/test/parity.mjs). Fields map to fm1-render's options; every engine and effect appears at least once. `cmd` is a sequencer verb script (fm1-render --cmd), relative to this file, at 64-frame blocks (#! block=64); it routes tracks with `route` verbs only, so track 0 plays the engine by the default-route rule. `panel` is panel input (fm1-sim-render --panel) with the lab switch on (`lab`): the render legs then play what the native harness logged (--log-cmds and its sidecar of arguments) instead of `cmd`.

scenarios.name: sophie-kit
scenarios.why: Sophie's feedback FM runs sinf/expf every sample; glibc's and musl's last-bit differences grow through the loop. A static musl build of fm1-render renders this byte for byte like the WebAssembly one (build-on-aeon.sh).

scenarios.name: sophie-clap-no-feedback
scenarios.why: Even without feedback, Sophie's envelopes and sweeps come from expf/exp2f/powf per voice and sinf per sample; a last-bit difference moves a clap burst by a sample. Identical to static musl.

scenarios.name: seq-capture-stopped-capsel
scenarios.why: Capture's stopped tempo search scores each candidate tempo with logf (seq_capture.c); a last-bit difference between glibc's logf and musl's could reorder near-tied candidates and so the take. Identical to static musl and to fm1-render.js.

scenarios.name: seq-panel-play-stop
scenarios.why: The panel drives the sequencer (docs/15 S3, the lab switch on): the module presses the buttons and turns the encoders; the render legs replay the commands and knob turns the native harness logged (--log-cmds and its .args sidecar), so this is also two-step parity.

scenarios.name: seq-panel-step-entry
scenarios.why: Step entry from the panel (docs/15 S4, the lab switch on): taps with a chord from MIDI IN, a probability, a condition and an invert on the Step pages, a second bar, a nudge, a pitch added with SHIFT and a step cleared with a SHIFT tap, then two passes of the two-bar clip. The render legs replay what the native harness logged (--log-cmds and its .args sidecar, with the MIDI IN notes); the module presses the same keys and buttons and plays the same notes.

scenarios.name: seq-panel-record
scenarios.why: Record and Capture from the panel (docs/15 S5, the lab switch on): REC with a bar's count-in and two keys recorded into the take, step record with a chord tied over two steps, a rest and a note at MIDI IN, then three keys captured while playing (SHIFT + REC). The keys' notes reach the sequencer as live input; the render legs replay them as the `non` and `nof` ops the native harness logged, with the keys' notes in its .args sidecar.

scenarios.name: seq-panel-capture-stopped
scenarios.why: A stopped Capture from the panel (docs/15 S5): six keys, then SHIFT + REC; the core reads the tempo, starts the transport and opens its picker, SELECT takes another tempo and a key closes it. The tempo search scores candidates with logf (seq_capture.c), as seq-capture-stopped-capsel; identical to static musl and to fm1-render.js.

scenarios.name: seq-metro-click
scenarios.why: The metronome's click (docs/15 S6, owner decision O11): a deterministic, integer-only click voice in the shared bridge (fm1_seq_click_mix), sounding each CLICK event while `metro` is on, added after the effects and before the limiter by fm1-render and the app alike: on while a bar plays, off, on again with swing, and a REC count-in after a stop.

scenarios.name: seq-panel-tracks
scenarios.why: Tracks from the panel (docs/15 S6, the lab switch on): SEQ + a white key focuses track 2, its Track page routes it to Sound 2 (Shapes), MUTE held with a white key mutes track 4, the Set page sets swing and tempo, track 2's Clip page plays it at 1/2X and 2X, SHIFT + 6 turns the metronome's click on and off, and a MUTE tap mutes track 2. The render legs replay the harness's log (`watch`, `route`, `mute`, `swing`, `bpm`, `cscl`, `metro`) with --slots, so this is two-step parity across tracks and sound units.

scenarios.name: seq-panel-locks
scenarios.why: Parameter locks from the panel (docs/15 S8, the lab switch on): a held step's lock page locks Timbre and Morph on step 5 and Harmonics on step 13 (`alabel`, `abase`, a quiet `aset`); playing, KNOB3 with no step held turns Timbre on its 7-bit grid and its lane's base follows (`abaseq`, and the knob's value replayed as --param-at); a stop just after step 5's locks sends each lane back to its base (D6), and PLAY plays on from there. The render legs replay the harness's log, so this is two-step parity for locks, base sync and the D6 revert.

scenarios.name: multi-two-sounds-inserts
scenarios.why: Multi-sound (docs/15 §3.16, the lab switch on): Macro as Sound 1 through a Crush insert at 80 %, Shapes as Sound 2 through Diffuse and Ensemble at 60 %, summed and through the master Plate. Notes on each sound (--note on Sound 1, --sound-note on Sound 2); the render legs run fm1-render --slots with the same units.

scenarios.name: multi-four-sounds-seq
scenarios.why: Four tracks routed to four slots (`route t 1 k`, docs/15 §3.16): Macro, Shapes and Six-Op as Sounds 1, 2 and 4, Sound 3 empty, so track 2 plays nothing; each sound renders split at its own tracks' events (fm1_seq_host_dispatch_slots) through its own inserts and level, and each lock lane resolves on its own track's sound (Shapes' Color, Six-Op's Brightness, Macro's Timbre).

scenarios.name: multi-panel
scenarios.why: Multi-sound from the panel (docs/15 §3.16): SHIFT + PRESETS makes Sound 2 current, a key and a MIDI IN note play it, KNOB2 turns its Timbre, the Mix page sets both levels, and SHIFT + PRESETS goes back to Sound 1, while two tracks play the two sounds. The render legs replay the harness's log and sidecar (--sound-note, --sound-param-at, --level-at), so this is two-step parity across sound units.
